## Brief
Objective: review the SPD-030 shell model rewrite on branch worktree-spd-030-bash-hook-cd-wrappers before Eric merges it. It is about 670 changed lines in the Bash hook, the code that enforces Laws 1, 5, 6 and 7, and it went well beyond its brief (a ShellWalk replacing split_segments, candidate working directories, six further parser fixes). Your verdict decides whether it merges as is, merges after fixes, or goes back. You change no code.

What to review, against `spud ticket show SPD-030` and `spud member show SPUD-030/Elba` (its brief and its Result, which lists every decision and the shell probe behind it):
1. Bypasses (most important). Try to build commands the new hook allows that, run by zsh or bash, write into ledger/ or reports/ for a member whose globs do not cover them, write outside a member's deliverables, or run a git write (commit, push, add, reset, ...) for a member. Aim at the new code: the walk over operators, subshell, group, if/case/loop/function frames, and-or lists, pipelines, background jobs, heredocs, newline and comment handling, process and command substitution, the candidate-directory set and when it collapses to None, the wrapper table and its value options, `env -S`, `script -c`, CDPATH, tildes, `cd old new`. Every claimed bypass needs a payload that the new hook allows and a real-shell probe (in the scratchpad, never against the live ledger or repository) showing the write or git effect.
2. Regressions. A differential run: the same corpus of commands through the hook on origin/main and on the branch, same scratch SPUD_HOME and bound member as the tests use. Report every command whose decision changed, and classify each as a hole closed, a new false refusal, or a new hole. Build the corpus from the existing tests in tests/test_hooks.py plus ordinary commands Spud and members really run (the spud calls in CLAUDE.md and the brief template, python3.14 test runs, git read commands, cd into a worktree then spud, heredocs to `spud ... @-`, pipes into grep/sed/head, `for` loops, `$(...)` in arguments). A new false refusal of normal work is a finding, not a detail.
3. Correctness of the decisions in Elba's Result: spot-check the shell claims you doubt with your own zsh 5.9 and bash 3.2 probes.
4. Robustness: can any input make the new walk raise, loop, or run slowly (deep nesting, long lines, unbalanced parentheses or quotes, huge heredocs)? A PreToolUse hook that raises must fail closed; confirm what happens.
5. Tests and code: do the new tests pin what they claim (would they fail if the fix were reverted piecewise)? Is the new code maintainable next to the rest of bin/spud_ledger.py (dead code left from split_segments, duplicated logic, names)? Keep this section short; bypasses and regressions come first.
